articles.title: Dean says he always applied laws - but which matches did he play games in?
articles.summary: Is there any evidence that former Premier League referee Mike Dean used to play mini-games during matches? BBC Sport has taken a look at the evidence.
body: Former Premier League referee Mike Dean says he did not intend to "undermine the integrity of refereeing" after claiming that he used to play mini-games to amuse himself during matches.
Dean had told Jamie Vardy's podcast that he would try to go as long as possible without blowing his whistle, or stay standing in the centre circle.
"We used to say, 'we'll kick off now. Right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle'," Dean said.
"I've done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously - went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle."

articles.title: Cathy Engelbert’s WNBA tenure: the wins and losses that defined her seven years
articles.summary: From record growth and a landmark media deal to expansion, labor battles and a fractured relationship with players, Engelbert’s tenure was rarely quiet. WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert will retire from the role on 30 December, bringing an end to a tenure that began with her appointment as the…
body: “After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner,” Engelbert said in a statement shared by the league. “In 2019, I had the privilege of being appointed the league’s first commissioner and to lead a league with enormous potential yet untapped awareness and significant undervaluation. Over the years, it has been amazing to watch WNBA players thrive and lead the massive cultural surge around women’s sports.”

Engelbert has not always been popular with players or fans. Her tenure has featured landmark successes as well as bruising controversies. Here is a look at some of the defining moments of her seven years leading the WNBA.

Engelbert was thrust into the fire almost immediately when the Covid-19 pandemic threatened her first season in charge. She helped oversee the creation of the “Wubble” at IMG Academy in Florida, allowing the league to stage a shortened 22-game season in 2020. The regular-season schedule has since expanded to 44 games and will grow to 50 in 2027.

articles.title: McLaren and Alpine F1 teams at odds after Briatore outburst over appeal
articles.summary: Briatore on the attack over Monaco GP decision. Accusation of judge’s bias towards McLaren. A furious row has broken out in the buildup to the Italian Grand Prix between the Alpine team executive adviser and de facto team principal, Flavio Briatore, and the McLaren principal, Andrea Stella, after…
body: Early on Friday a decision was released by the court of appeal, finding in favour of McLaren and Red Bull appeals against the result of the Monaco GP, prompted by a series of pit lane speeding penalties that were incorrect. The pit lane at Monaco had been incorrectly measured, leading to the penalties, including two for Alpine’s Pierre Gasly. Alpine appealed against those and they were successful, with the Frenchman subsequently awarded third place.

However, that decision went to the court of appeal who reversed the decision, demoting Gasly to seventh, with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar returned to his third place and McLaren’s Oscar Piastri to fourth.

Briatore, who had a lifetime Formula One ban for fixing the 2008 Singapore Grand Prix overturned, arrived for the press conferenceon Friday in Monza with an A4 piece of paper and, sitting across from Stella, immediately launched into an attack on the judgment, claiming it had been biased.

articles.title: Price puts Glos back in contention against Derbys
articles.summary: Ollie Price produces a career-best bowling performance to put Gloucestershire back in contention on day three of the County Championship match against Derbyshire.
body: Ollie Price produced a career-best bowling performance to put Gloucestershire back in contention on day three of the County Championship Second Division match against Derbyshire in Bristol.

Gloucestershire prepared a pitch for their overseas spinner Sai Kishore, only for the Indian international to be upstaged by Price, who took 6-45 from 21.4 overs with his off breaks as Derbyshire were bowled out for 278, a first-innings lead of 41.
Matt Montgomery scored a fluent 65, only for the visitors to suffer a startling collapse, their last eight wickets falling for just 74 runs.

Joe Phillips then posted a patient 65 and shared in a third-wicket stand of 69 with Miles Hammond (46*) as Gloucestershire, making a decent fist of things in their second innings, reached 149-3 by the close, a lead of 108. Shoaib Bashir has taken 2-59 and Derbyshire will look to the England spinner to make further inroads in the morning.

articles.title: 'It's so strong' - Sabalenka halts play over cannabis smell
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka briefly halts her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of the smell of cannabis before going on to reach the fourth round.
body: Aryna Sabalenka briefly halted her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova because of a strong smell of cannabis before cruising into the fourth round in New York.
Top seed Sabalenka raised the issue after going 3-0 up in the first set against Uzbekistan's Rakhimova, telling umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore that "someone is smoking weed".
Asderaki-Moore spoke to an official on her radio and made a smoking gesture to someone behind her, before play continued.
Two-time defending champion Sabalenka went on to secure a confident 6-3 6-4 victory on Louis Armstrong Stadium as she chases a fifth Grand Slam singles title.

articles.title: Ferrari still behind Mercedes on straights - Hamilton
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari's new engine is "an improvement" but that his team are still lagging behind Mercedes on the straights at the Italian Grand Prix.
body: Mercedes' George Russell topped Friday practice at the Italian Grand Prix by 0.120 seconds from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.
Hamilton was fifth, 0.457secs off the pace, and also behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.
"Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into," Hamilton said.
It is unlikely that Ferrari were using the full performance of their new engine on its first day of running, and Antonelli gave a different analysis of his rivals' pace.

articles.title: Takeaways from Colorado football's comeback win over Georgia Tech
articles.summary: Colorado took down Georgia Tech behind a physical run game and strong defense. Here are five takeaways from the Buffaloes' season-opening victory
body: Before Colorado's 14-13 win over Georgia Tech in their season opener, they had not defeated an ACC team since the Orange Bowl back on Jan. 1, 1957, against Clemson. While this is an impressive feat for the program, what might be more impressive is how the Buffaloes won this game.

Colorado established their offensive identity as a team that will dominate the line of scrimmage and run the ball down opponents' throats. They finished the game with 48 rushing attempts, their most since 49 against Northern Colorado in 2021.

Quarterback Julian Lewis led the game-winning drive in the final two minutes of the game. But before that point, Lewis struggled. Decision-making was not a problem, as he put the ball in the right place and never made any errant throws that could have led to an interception. However, it was clear he was not on the same page as his receivers at times and missed open receivers downfield. Luckily, in this offense, Lewis does not need to carry the franchise. But he still needs to improve his communication and accuracy downfield. Once he does, Lewis has the potential to be an elite quarterback in college football this season.

articles.title: 49ers’ Keion White opens up about ‘trauma’ of gunshot wound recovery
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Keion White has opened up about the difficult recovery from a gunshot wound to his right ankle. White was shot during an altercation at a San Francisco nightclub in the early hours after NFL Super Bowl 60.
body: “ It’s different because it’s trauma instead of just, like, breaking an ankle with a sports-related injury,” White said, via The Athletic. “When you hurt yourself in football, there’s a protocol for damn near everything.”
Then he said, “Football players don’t just get shot every day,” while mentioning, “I mean, I guess they do on this team,” referring to the incident involving Ricky Pearsall.
White, 27, tried to keep the situation light despite the severity of the injury. He said he was joking while being taken to the hospital and did not realize he had been shot immediately.
Still, he clearly said that the incident remains unusual, “But, yeah … it’s not a normal thing, getting shot.”

articles.title: 'It's going to be tight' - Hamilton eyes 'dream' Monza pole
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton is predicting a “very close” battle in Italian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday for what he says would he says would be a “dream” pole position at Monza.
body: Hamilton was outperformed by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in both of Friday's practice sessions but the team's overall performance, following the arrival of a new engine upgrade, suggested they have the pace to compete for pole.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.
"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.

articles.title: SAFC takes on Tulsa in showdown with playoff implications
articles.summary: A showdown for one of the top four spots in the USL Championship Western Conference table will be at stake when San Antonio FC hosts FC Tulsa on Saturday at Toyota Field.
body: SAFC (9-5-8, 32 points), fifth in the conference standings, and Tulsa (10-6-5, 35 points), which is ahead of San Antonio in fourth place, kick off at 7:30 p.m.

With eight games remaining in the regular season, SAFC is trying to climb up the Western table, as nabbing one of the top four spots would allow the club to host a first-round playoff game. The USL Championship playoffs start in November.

SAFC's playoff chances got a big boost last Saturday in Albuquerque after a 2-1 win over New Mexico United. With the victory, San Antonio knocked New Mexico out of first place in the Western Conference standings and halted the United's 13-match unbeaten streak. It was New Mexico's first loss since May.

The big win came at the right time for SAFC, which had lost two straight games at home coming into the New Mexico match and had been shutout in both matches, the first time this season San Antonio had lost two consecutive matches at Toyota Field and had been shutout in back-to-back games on its home pitch.

articles.title: Usman Nurmagomedov hasn’t yet fought in the UFC, yet he’s been a recurring main event for the past month
articles.summary: You know how you can tell when somebody’s on the verge of extracting the prize from prizefighting? It’s when they begin to dominate headlines without ever throwing a punch. Enter: Usman Nurmagomedov.
body: Oh, Usman Nurmagomedov came close to doing just that in his first unofficial Octagon visit. Last weekend in Shanghai he hopped the fence like a thief in the night after Song Yadong sent his older brother Umar “to the land of wind and ghosts,” as my colleague Ben Fowlkes likes to say, loading up as if deliver an elbow as Song did his victory lap. Fortunately, he didn’t do it, yet that semi-action — which Usman himself said was much ado about nothing — helped him generate more headlines than Song.

A couple of weeks prior, out in Philadelphia, Usman was shown on the UFC 330 broadcast sitting cageside, the first indications that the UFC is biding its time until it can sign him. It might’ve been the most exciting thing about the event. The word being tossed around about the world’s top MMA free agent signing with the UFC has been “inevitable” ever since, which feels a little Calvinistic for a man of free will.

articles.title: Stella fumes at 'insulting' Briatore allegations after Alpine lose podium
articles.summary: Andrea Stella has accused Alpine chief Flavio Briatore of "insulting" McLaren by questioning the relationship between the reigning constructors' champions and a judge at the FIA's International Court of Appeal.
body: The court announced on Friday that penalties given to Alpine driver Pierre Gasly during June's Monaco Grand Prix would be reinstated, following a successful appeal by McLaren and Red Bull.

Gasly took the chequered flag in third but was demoted when two five-second penalties for speeding in the pit lane were applied at that point. However, a right of review appeal from Alpine saw the penalties withdrawn five days later.
The reinstatement of the penalty drops Gasly back to seventh in the official classification. Red Bull's Isack Hadjar gets a podium in third, while McLaren's Oscar Piastri moves up to fourth.

In an explosive press conference at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, which coincidentally featured Alpine executive director Briatore and McLaren team principal Stella, the pair engaged in a remarkable clash.

articles.title: Sabalenka beats Rakhimova to reach fourth round of US Open
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka came through a tough test against Kamilla Rakhimova - particularly in the second set - to reach the fourth round of the US Open.
body: The two-time defending champion in New York started superbly, storming into a 3-0 lead in the opening set as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce.
That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second.

Sabalenka would cut a frustrated figure as Rakhimova came from behind four-straight times to hold serve, saving four break points along the way, before the world No 1 finally ended her resolve in the ninth game of the second set.
On this occasion, Rakhimova let a 40-0 lead slip as Sabalenka battled back to secure the crucial break before serving things out to book her spot in the last 16.
